about: House recipes, batch 04 (helper sA): written by Claude in a Max-plan session, original, ai-draft. Nutrition is a per-serve estimate kept as data only.

recipes.title: Bacalhau com Natas (Portuguese Cod and Potato Bake with Cream)
recipes.summary: Flaked salt-free white fish, soft onion and potato layered in a creamy sauce and baked until golden.
steps: Poach the fish in simmering water for 5 minutes, until it flakes. Drain, then flake into large pieces, removing any bones.
Cook the potato in boiling salted water for 8 minutes, until just tender. Drain well.

Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes. Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and cream. Simmer for 4 minutes, until thick, then add nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Layer potato, onion and fish in a baking dish, pour over the sauce and top with the mozzarella.
Bake for 20 minutes, until bubbling and golden. Scatter with parsley and serve.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Fresh fish is used here instead of salt cod, so no soaking is needed.

recipes.title: Bacalhau à Brás (Portuguese Shredded Cod with Egg and Potato)
recipes.summary: Flaked fish, soft onion and crisp potato strands bound with softly scrambled egg.
steps: Poach the fish in simmering water for 5 minutes, until it flakes. Drain and flake, removing any bones.
Dry the potato well. Fry in the oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat for 10 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. Lift out and drain.
In the same pan, soften the onion and garlic for 8 minutes with a pinch of salt.
Add the fish and potato and toss for 2 minutes. Beat the eggs with pepper, pour in and stir over low heat for 3 minutes, until just set and creamy.
Scatter with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.

Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set; avoid runny eggs for pregnant, elderly, very young or immune-compromised eaters. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Arroz de Pato (Portuguese Duck Rice)
recipes.summary: Shredded braised duck baked through rice with smoky chorizo until the top turns crisp.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Put the duck, onion, garlic, bay leaves, wine and 2 cups water in a lidded casserole, cover and braise for 1 1/2 hours, until the meat falls from the bone.
Lift out the duck, strain the juices and shred the meat, discarding skin and bones. Skim the fat from the juices.
Fry the chorizo in the oil for 3 minutes. Add the rice and stir for 1 minute, then add the stock and 1 cup of the duck juices.
Cover and bake for 20 minutes, until the rice is tender. Fold in most of the duck.
Top with the rest of the duck and the chorizo. Bake uncovered for 10 minutes, until crisp on top, then scatter with parsley.
notes: Food safety: duck must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Cool leftover rice quickly and eat within a day.
Dairy-free.

recipes.title: Porco à Alentejana (Portuguese Pork and Clams)
recipes.summary: Marinated pork pieces fried then tossed with clams, paprika and fried potato cubes.
steps: Toss the pork with the paprika, garlic, wine, bay leaves and salt. Marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
Fry the potato in half the oil for 12 minutes, until golden. Drain and set aside.
Drain the pork, saving the marinade. Fry in the remaining oil over high heat for 10 minutes, until browned. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the marinade and bring to a boil. Add the clams, cover and cook for 5 minutes, until the shells open. Discard any that stay shut.
Fold in the potato and coriander and serve with lemon.
notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Boil the marinade for the full time or discard it; never serve it raw.

recipes.title: Bitoque (Portuguese Steak with Fried Egg and Chips)
recipes.summary: A thin pan-fried steak in garlicky wine sauce, topped with a fried egg and served with chips and rice.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan). Toss the chips with the oil and salt on a tray and roast for 30 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Season the steaks. Fry in half the butter over high heat for 2 minutes each side. Rest on a plate.
Add the garlic, wine and bay leaves to the pan, simmer for 3 minutes, then whisk in the remaining butter with any resting juices.
Fry the eggs in a little oil for 3 minutes, until the whites are set.
Plate each steak with rice and chips, pour over the sauce and top with an egg. Serve with lemon.
notes: Food safety: whole steaks are safe seared medium-rare, but cook any minced or rolled beef to 75°C. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set; avoid runny eggs for pregnant, elderly, very young or immune-compromised eaters. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Feijoada à Transmontana (Portuguese Pork and Bean Stew)
recipes.summary: Slow-cooked beans with pork, smoked sausage and cabbage in a thick, comforting stew.
steps: Brown the pork and chorizo in the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat for 8 minutes. Add the onion, garlic and carrot and cook for 6 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, paprika and bay leaves for 1 minute, then add the stock. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes, until the pork is tender.
Add the beans and cabbage and cook uncovered for 15 minutes, until the stew has thickened.
Season to taste and finish with parsley. Serve with crusty bread.
notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free. Better the next day.

recipes.title: Khachapuri Adjaruli (Georgian Cheese Boat with Egg)
recipes.summary: A boat of soft dough filled with melted cheese, finished with an egg and a knob of butter.
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and 1 tsp salt. Stir in the milk and oil to form a dough, knead for 8 minutes, then cover and leave until doubled, about 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 240°C (220°C fan) with a tray inside. Mix the mozzarella, feta and 1 egg.
Divide the dough into 4. Roll each into an oval, roll the long edges inward and pinch the ends to form a boat. Fill with the cheese mix.

Bake on the hot tray for 12 minutes, until the crust is golden. Make a well in each filling, drop in an egg yolk (save the whites for another dish) and bake for 2 minutes more, so the yolk stays soft.
Top each with butter, stir the yolk into the cheese at the table and tear off pieces of crust to dip.
notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set; avoid runny eggs for pregnant, elderly, very young or immune-compromised eaters. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten, milk and egg. The yolk is left soft, so leave it out if eaters are pregnant or vulnerable.

recipes.title: Chakhokhbili (Georgian Chicken and Tomato Stew)
recipes.summary: Chicken braised in its own juices with tomato, onion and a big handful of fresh herbs.
steps: Brown the chicken in the oil in a heavy pot for 8 minutes, skin side down first. Lift out.
Cook the onion in the pot for 8 minutes. Add the tomato, garlic and spices and cook for 5 minutes, until it breaks down.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer on low for 30 minutes, until cooked through and tender.
Stir in half the herbs and season. Scatter the rest over and serve with bread or rice.
notes: Food safety: chicken must reach 75°C in the thickest part with no pink juices. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Lobio (Georgian Kidney Bean Stew with Walnuts)
recipes.summary: Spiced kidney beans mashed to a thick stew with walnuts, coriander and fenugreek, eaten with cornbread.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil for 10 minutes, until deep golden.
Add the garlic, spices and walnuts and stir for 1 minute.
Add the beans and water, simmer for 20 minutes, mashing about a third with a spoon, until thick.
Stir in the vinegar and half the coriander, season, and scatter the rest over. Serve with bread.
notes: Canned beans are already cooked; if using dried kidney beans, soak overnight and boil hard for 10 minutes first.
Vegan and dairy-free. Contains walnuts.

recipes.title: Chashushuli (Georgian Beef and Tomato Stew)
recipes.summary: Beef simmered with tomato, onion, garlic and fresh herbs until rich and spoonable.
steps: Brown the beef in batches in the oil for 8 minutes, until deeply coloured. Lift out.
Cook the onion for 8 minutes, then add garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Return the beef with the tomatoes and water. Cover and simmer on low for 1 hour, until very tender.
Stir through the herbs, season and serve with bread or rice.
notes: Food safety: beef pieces are safe once they reach at least 70°C and are tender; braise until the meat pulls apart. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Kibinai (Lithuanian Lamb Pasties)
recipes.summary: Half-moon pastries filled with lamb, onion and herbs, a Karaite Lithuanian speciality.
steps: Rub the cold butter into the flour with 1/2 tsp salt. Mix in the sour cream and egg to a dough, wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Soften the onion in the butter for 6 minutes. Mix with the lamb, marjoram, dill, salt and pepper.
Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Roll the dough 3mm thick and cut 12cm rounds. Put filling on each, fold over and pinch the edge to seal.
Brush with the egg yolk and bake for 25 minutes, until golden and the filling is cooked through.
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve warm.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten, egg and dairy.

recipes.title: Cepelinai (Lithuanian Potato Dumplings with Pork)
recipes.summary: Large grated-potato dumplings around a seasoned pork centre, served with bacon and sour cream.
steps: Grate 2/3 of the potato and squeeze it in a cloth, saving the starchy liquid. Boil the remaining potato for 15 minutes, mash, and mix with the raw grated potato, the settled starch from the liquid and 1 tsp salt.
Mix the pork, half the onion, garlic, marjoram, salt and pepper.
Wet your hands, flatten some potato mix in your palm, put a spoon of pork in the middle and shape into an oval, sealing completely. Make 8.
Simmer gently in salted water for 30 minutes, until firm. Don't let the water boil hard or they'll break up.
Fry the bacon and remaining onion in the butter until golden. Serve the dumplings with the bacon, sour cream and dill.
notes: Food safety: pork mince must reach 75°C in the centre; cut one open to check. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.

recipes.title: Kugelis (Lithuanian Baked Potato Pudding with Bacon)
recipes.summary: A grated-potato bake studded with bacon and onion, crusty on top and soft inside.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C (170°C fan) and butter a 22cm baking dish.
Fry the bacon and onion in a pan for 8 minutes, until golden. Cool slightly.
Grate the potato and drain off the liquid. Mix with the eggs, milk, bacon and onion, salt and pepper.
Pour into the dish and bake for 1 hour, until deep golden and set through.
Rest for 5 minutes. Serve in squares with sour cream and dill.
notes: Food safety: bacon and eggs should be fully cooked; the centre should be firm and hot. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Gluten-free.

recipes.title: Karjalanpiirakka with Egg Butter (Karelian Rice Pasties)
recipes.summary: Thin rye shells filled with creamy rice porridge, served with egg butter, a Finnish classic.
steps: Simmer the rice with the milk and water for 30 minutes, stirring often, until a thick porridge. Season well.
Mix both flours, 1/2 tsp salt, the water and oil into a firm dough and rest for 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 250°C (230°C fan). Roll the dough into 12 thin rounds about 12cm wide, put porridge in the middle and fold the edges in to make an oval.
Bake for 15 minutes, until the edges are browned. Brush with melted butter.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, until the yolks are firm. Peel, mash with the soft butter and salt and serve on warm pasties.
notes: Food safety: eggs should be cooked until the whites are fully set; avoid runny eggs for pregnant, elderly, very young or immune-compromised eaters. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten, egg and dairy.

recipes.title: Janssons Frestelse (Swedish Potato and Anchovy Gratin)
recipes.summary: Thin potato matchsticks baked with sweet onion, anchovies and cream until golden.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Soften the onion in half the butter for 8 minutes.
Layer potato, onion and anchovies in a buttered dish, finishing with potato.
Mix the cream, milk and 1 tbsp of the anchovy oil; pour over, scatter with breadcrumbs and dot with the remaining butter.
Bake for 50 minutes, until the potato is tender and the top is deep golden.
Rest 5 minutes and scatter with dill.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Main course in Sweden, often with a green salad on the side.

recipes.title: Frikadeller (Danish Pork Meatballs with Potatoes and Gravy)
recipes.summary: Pan-fried pork meatballs seasoned with onion and allspice, served with boiled potatoes and brown gravy.
steps: Mix the pork, onion, egg, 1/2 cup flour, milk, allspice, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Chill for 15 minutes if time allows.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes, until tender.
Shape the pork mix into 12 oval balls. Fry in half the butter over medium heat for 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through. Lift out.
Whisk the 2 tbsp flour into the pan juices, then the stock, and simmer for 5 minutes into a gravy.
Serve with potatoes and gravy, sprinkled with parsley.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

recipes.title: Flæskesteg (Danish Roast Pork with Crackling)
recipes.summary: A Danish Sunday roast of pork loin with crisp crackling, bay and cloves, served with red cabbage and potatoes.

items: 1.5 kg pork loin, skin on, scored

steps: Dry the pork skin, rub with the salt and leave uncovered in the fridge for 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 230°C (210°C fan). Push the cloves into the meat and tuck bay leaves into the scoring. Sit on the onion in a tin.
Roast for 25 minutes, then turn down to 180°C (160°C fan) and cook for 1 1/2 hours, until the meat reaches 70°C and the skin is crisp.
Rest for 15 minutes. Meanwhile boil the potatoes for 20 minutes.
Whisk the flour into the pan juices, add the stock and simmer for 5 minutes. Carve and serve with gravy and potatoes.
notes: Food safety: pork must reach at least 70°C in the centre, with clear juices, and rest before serving. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free. Add pickled red cabbage on the side if you like.

recipes.title: Fårikål (Norwegian Lamb and Cabbage Stew)
recipes.summary: Norway's national dish: lamb and cabbage layered in a pot with whole pepper and simmered gently.

items: 1.2 kg lamb shoulder, bone in, cut in pieces

steps: Layer the lamb and cabbage in a heavy pot, sprinkling flour, peppercorns and salt between the layers.
Pour in the water, cover and bring to a simmer. Cook gently for 2 hours, until the lamb is tender and falling off the bone.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes.
Serve in deep bowls with the lamb, cabbage, broth and potatoes.
notes: Food safety: lamb pieces should reach at least 70°C and be tender. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Dairy-free. Even better the next day.

recipes.title: Kjøttkaker (Norwegian Meatball Patties in Brown Gravy)
recipes.summary: Spiced beef and pork patties in a creamy brown gravy with potatoes, peas and lingonberry jam.
steps: Mix the beef, pork, onion, egg, milk, 1/4 cup flour, spices, 1 tsp salt and pepper. Shape into 8 flat patties.
Fry in half the butter for 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through. Lift out.
Whisk the 2 tbsp flour into the pan with the remaining butter, add the stock and simmer for 8 minutes into a gravy.
Boil the potatoes for 20 minutes, adding the peas for the last 3.
Serve the patties with gravy, potatoes, peas and jam.
notes: Food safety: mince must reach 75°C in the centre with no pink inside. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains gluten, egg and milk.

recipes.title: Pasta alla Gricia (Roman Guanciale and Pecorino Pasta)
recipes.summary: The cacio e pepe and amatriciana's older cousin: crisp cured pork, pecorino and black pepper.
steps: Boil the pasta in well-salted water until al dente, saving 1 cup of the cooking water.
Fry the pancetta in a large pan over medium heat for 8 minutes, until crisp, with the pepper for the last minute.
Add the pasta and 1/2 cup of the water to the pan and toss over low heat for 1 minute.
Take off the heat, add the pecorino and toss, adding more water as needed until the sauce is glossy and clings to the pasta. Serve at once.
notes: Food safety: cured pork like pancetta should be cooked until crisp and eaten the same day, or refrigerated within an hour. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains pecorino, a hard cheese that usually isn't vegetarian, gluten and milk.

recipes.title: Risotto alla Milanese (Saffron Risotto)
recipes.summary: The golden risotto of Milan, scented with saffron and finished with butter and vegetarian hard cheese.
steps: Steep the saffron in 1/4 cup of the hot stock.
Melt half the butter in a wide pan and cook the onion for 6 minutes, until soft. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble away. Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18 to 20 minutes, adding the saffron liquid halfway.
When the rice is creamy and just tender, take off the heat. Stir in the remaining butter and the vegetarian hard cheese, cover and rest for 2 minutes.
Serve straight away on warm plates.
notes: Vegetarian. Serves four as a main or six as a side with osso buco.
Gluten-free.

recipes.title: Risotto ai Funghi Misti (Mixed Mushroom Risotto)
recipes.summary: Earthy mushrooms folded through creamy rice with thyme and vegetarian hard cheese.
steps: Fry the mushrooms in the oil over high heat in two batches for 6 minutes each, until golden. Season and set aside.
Melt half the butter, cook the onion and garlic for 5 minutes, then stir in the rice and thyme for 2 minutes.
Add the wine, then the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 18 to 20 minutes.
Fold in the mushrooms, remaining butter and vegetarian hard cheese. Rest for 2 minutes.
Serve topped with parsley.
notes: Vegetarian. Gluten-free.

recipes.title: Risotto alla Pescatora (Seafood Risotto)
recipes.summary: Creamy rice with prawns, mussels and white fish in a light tomato and white wine base.
steps: Soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the rice and stir for 2 minutes, then the wine.
Add the tomatoes, then the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 15 minutes.
Add the fish and cook 3 minutes, then the prawns and mussels, cover and cook for 4 minutes, until the prawns are pink and the mussels open. Discard any that stay shut.
Rest for 2 minutes, then stir in the lemon juice and parsley.
Serve straight away; no cheese is added.
notes: Food safety: fish is cooked when it turns opaque and flakes easily; cook shellfish until shells open or flesh is opaque and discard any that stay shut. Eat the same day or refrigerate within an hour and use within 24 hours.
Contains shellfish and fish. Dairy-free and gluten-free.

recipes.title: Risi e Bisi (Venetian Rice and Pea Stew)
recipes.summary: A thick Venetian rice and pea dish with pancetta, somewhere between a soup and a risotto.
steps: Fry the pancetta in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute, then add the stock a ladle at a time for 12 minutes.
Add the peas and cook for 5 minutes more, until the rice is tender but the dish is still wet.
Stir in the butter, pecorino and parsley and serve in shallow bowls.
notes: Food safety: cured pork should be cooked until crisp and eaten the same day, or refrigerated within an hour. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Contains pecorino, a hard cheese that usually isn't vegetarian and milk.

recipes.title: Cotoletta alla Milanese (Milanese Crumbed Veal Cutlet)
recipes.summary: A thin veal cutlet crumbed and fried in butter until golden, served with lemon and rocket.
steps: Flatten the veal with a rolling pin to 6mm thick and season.
Dredge in the flour, dip in the beaten eggs, then press into the breadcrumbs.
Heat half the butter and oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Fry two cutlets at a time for 3 minutes each side, until deep golden and cooked through. Repeat with the rest.
Drain on paper and serve at once with rocket and lemon.
notes: Food safety: veal must reach 70°C in the centre with no pink. Cook the crumbed meat fully. Refrigerate leftovers within an hour and reheat until steaming hot.
Pork or chicken cutlets can be used instead.
